analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 1369-1381). It adds prose on Qwen inline MTP assistant behavior: ordinary decode rows chaining, hidden-state carry, a per-drafter opt-in (supportsOrdinaryDecodeHistory), and two rollback env switches (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY). The supplied units are BASE text ranges at lines 1638-2205, which contain no changed lines; the actual changed hunk is visible only in the patch excerpt. No code, authorization, attestation, encryption, cache-scope, or wire-contract change is in this batch. The documented behavior concerns speculative-decode assistant history and carry state inside the provider process. It does not touch the prefix-cache or SSD-tier controls in T-041 (HMAC names, TTL, salt scoping, KEK). Nor does it touch the coordinator-to-provider channel (TB-002), model weights or attestation. It also does not alter the fail-open-to-target-only MTP invariant (invariant 7). Residual questions for later passes: (1) the implementing code in EngineLoopV2+MTPOrdinaryHistory.swift and finalizeMTPOrdinaryHistory is not supplied. Whether carry or assistant-history state is scoped per request and cleared on cancel or retire, so it cannot leak across tenants (A-001, T-028), is unverified. (2) Whether the carry or hidden rows interact with the SSD complete-prefix checkpoint coding (CBv2MTPPrefixCheckpointCoding) without adding prompt-derived on-disk metadata is unverified. No concrete security regression can be established from documentation alone.
